title: The Power of Music
description: How music affects our mood, our bodies and our ability to learn.
instructions: Read the passage about music, then choose the best answer (A, B, C or D) for each question.

paragraphs.text: Music is found in every human culture, from ancient tribes to modern cities. People sing at weddings, play songs at parties and listen to music while they travel or exercise. Scientists have become increasingly interested in why music is so important to us. Their research suggests that music affects our bodies and minds in surprising ways.

One of the clearest effects of music is on our mood. A cheerful song can make us feel more energetic, while a slow, gentle melody can help us relax after a difficult day. When we listen to music we enjoy, the brain releases chemicals that make us feel good. This is one reason why many people reach for their headphones when they feel sad or anxious.

Music can also help with physical activity. Runners and cyclists often find that a song with a strong beat helps them keep a steady pace. Some studies suggest that people feel less tired when they exercise to music, even if they are working just as hard. In hospitals, music is sometimes used to calm patients before an operation or to help them recover.

Learning to play an instrument may bring further benefits. Children who take music lessons have to practise patience, listen carefully and remember long patterns of notes. Some researchers believe these skills can support learning in other subjects, although the evidence is not yet certain. What is clear is that music brings people together, whether they are singing in a choir or dancing at a concert.

Music is also closely connected to memory. Hearing a song from our teenage years can suddenly bring back the place we were, the people we were with and even how we felt at the time. Some care homes use this power to help elderly people with memory problems. Even when they struggle to recognise members of their own family, many of them can still sing along to songs they learned when they were young. For a few minutes, the music seems to wake up parts of the mind that were thought to be lost.

Many people like to listen to music while they work or study, but its effect seems to depend on the person and the task. For simple, repetitive jobs, music can make the time pass more quickly and keep people motivated. For tasks that need careful thought, such as reading a difficult text, songs with words may be distracting, because the brain tries to follow the lyrics as well. For this reason, some students prefer music without singing, while others need complete silence to concentrate.

Finally, technology has changed the way we listen. In the past, people bought records or waited for their favourite song to come on the radio. Today, streaming services offer millions of songs on a phone, often for a small monthly fee. Some critics worry that, with so much choice, we now treat music as background noise and rarely listen with full attention. Yet concerts and festivals remain as popular as ever, which suggests that people still value the experience of sharing music in the same place at the same time.

questions.text: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Music has many positive effects on people's minds and bodies.
Music lessons are the best way to improve school results.
Scientists do not understand why people like music.
Only some cultures enjoy music.
questions.explanation: The passage describes the effects of music on mood, exercise, health and learning.

evidence.quote: Their research suggests that music affects our bodies and minds in surprising ways.

questions.text: According to paragraph 2, what happens in the brain when we listen to music we enjoy?
options: It stops working for a short time.
It forgets sad memories.
It releases chemicals that make us feel good.
It becomes more tired.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 says the brain releases chemicals that make us feel good.

evidence.quote: the brain releases chemicals that make us feel good

questions.text: In paragraph 3, the word "steady" is closest in meaning to:
options: fast
regular and even
difficult
changing
questions.explanation: A steady pace is one that stays the same, regular and even.

evidence.quote: helps them keep a steady pace

questions.text: What can we infer from paragraph 3 about exercising to music?
options: It makes people work less hard.
It is only useful for professional athletes.
It is not allowed in hospitals.
It can make exercise feel easier.
questions.explanation: People feel less tired even though they work just as hard, so the exercise feels easier.

evidence.quote: people feel less tired when they exercise to music, even if they are working just as hard

questions.text: Why does the writer mention hospitals in paragraph 3?
options: To criticise how doctors treat patients
To give another example of music helping the body
To explain how operations are performed
To advertise a new type of medicine
questions.explanation: Hospitals are a further example of music having a physical benefit: calming patients and helping them recover.

evidence.quote: In hospitals, music is sometimes used to calm patients before an operation or to help them recover.

questions.text: What is the writer's attitude to the idea that music lessons improve learning in other subjects?
options: The writer is completely sure it is true.
The writer thinks it is a silly idea.
The writer says it has been proved wrong.
The writer is careful because the evidence is not yet certain.
questions.explanation: The writer says only that some researchers believe it, and that the evidence is not yet certain.

evidence.quote: although the evidence is not yet certain

Elderly people prefer old songs to new ones.

evidence.quote: Music is also closely connected to memory.
